title: Prefetch coordinator: latency-sensitivity tuning for paged/blocked KV cache
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a coordinator layer for prefetch and admission decisions targeted at paged/blocked KV cache deployments to reduce tail latency while preserving throughput for continuous batching workloads. This ticket captures design and implementation details for a latency-sensitive prefetch heuristic, admission throttles, and GPU residency hints that play nicely with our existing blocked KV pager and host-backed swap flow.
technical_design:
Background:
Our existing blocked KV cache slices model KV state into page-like blocks and evicts or stages blocks to host when GPU residency budgets are exceeded. Continuous batching increases overlap between requests and changes access patterns: repeated prefix hits create hotset pressure while long-context chat sessions produce temporal locality that our pager can exploit. Current blind prefetch (prefetch N next blocks) either overfetches and causes unnecessary host->GPU transfers, or underfetches and leaves requests hitting host and incurring 10–30ms tail penalties.

Coordinator goals:
1) Make prefetch decisions informed by per-request latency sensitivity, batch membership, and observed hotness statistics rather than fixed lookahead counts.
2) Avoid injecting jitter into token latency for low-latency SLO routes (interactive chat) while allowing aggressive prefetch for throughput-oriented routes (background embeddings or offline ranking).
3) Integrate admission control with continuous batching: prefer fetching blocks for the head-of-batch requests that are latency sensitive and deprioritize speculative fetches for tail-only throughput gains when GPU memory is constrained.

Core components:
- Route latency profile: annotate incoming requests with a latency_sensitivity score (low|medium|high) derived from route config and percentiles in Console. High-sensitivity requests are treated as single-shot and prioritized for on-GPU residency.
- Adaptive lookahead windows: maintain a per-tenant exponential moving average of forward/backward token jump distances. For each model+route, compute lookahead_size = clamp(base * hotness_factor * sensitivity_multiplier, 0, max_prefetch).
- Residency budget queue: each GPU maintains a soft budget for paged blocks that can be used for speculative prefetched blocks. If budget exhausted, coordinator falls back to an LRU steal policy and reduces lookahead for that tenant by a decay factor.
- Batch-aware scoring: when a batch is formed, compute marginal benefit of fetching a block as sum of sensitivity-weighted expected hit-rate improvement across requests in the batch. Use approximate heuristics to avoid O(n*m) scoring: maintain a bloom-like per-batch hotset summary derived from recent token traces.
- Background host transfer shaping: rate limit PCIe staging transfers using token-bucket tied to observed end-to-end request latency trends. When tail p50->p99 delta grows beyond threshold, throttle speculative transfers to preserve interactive SLOs.

Implementation notes:
- Expose new route config fields: latency_profile (interactive|balanced|throughput), prefetch_max (int), prefetch_budget_fraction (0.0-1.0). Defaults chosen to preserve backward compatibility.
- Extend existing KV pager metadata to add last_access_sketch (compact timestamped counters) and tenant_prefetch_state. These are kept on host memory and are not serialized to checkpoints.
- Integrate with scheduler: prefetch operations are scheduled as I/O-priority tasks and annotated to the GPU swap coordinator so we can preempt speculative fetches if a high-sensitivity request arrives.
acceptance_criteria: New coordinator routes can be enabled per-tenant via route config without restart
P99 latency on interactive routes decreases by at least 8% under mixed workload compared to baseline prefetching=false
Overall GPU memory oversubscription events remain within current SLA during stress tests (no >5% increase)
Unit and integration tests for lookahead computation, budget enforcement, and batch scoring are added
Feature flag exists to roll back coordinator quickly in production
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag with defaults off. 2) Canary on internal staging cluster with synthetic mixed workloads to validate metrics. 3) Gradual ramp to 5% production traffic for tenants opted-in, monitor p50/p95/p99 and GPU OOM metrics for 48h. 4) Raise to 25% and then 100% once thresholds are stable. 5) If tail latency regresses beyond threshold or OOMs spike, flip feature flag off and run automated postmortem checks.
testing_plan: Unit tests: lookahead math, sensitivity multipliers, budget decay. Integration tests: simulated continuous-batching harness with mixed latency profiles; verify prefetch no-op when budget exhausted. Load tests: run mixed workloads (interactive chat + batch embeddings) on staging with artificially constrained GPU memory and PCIe bandwidth to validate transfer shaping. Chaos tests: inject high-sensitivity request bursts and confirm prefetch preemption and transfer throttling behaviors.
risks:
- Incorrect sensitivity scoring could starve throughput workloads if we bias too heavily to interactive traffic.
- Prefetch misestimation could increase PCIe transfer volume and saturate host->GPU links.
- Tenant metadata growth (last_access_sketch) increases host memory usage if not compacted.
- Complex batch scoring may add CPU overhead to the batching pipeline; need to keep heuristics O(1) per-request on average.
notes:
Design trade-offs considered: we rejected full per-block access counters due to RAM cost and opted for compact sketches bounded to ~256 bytes/tenant/model. We considered using a learned predictor (small LRU-ML model) but deferred to heuristics to reduce iteration risk.

Telemetry to add: prefetch_hit_rate by route and tenant, prefetch_transfer_bytes, prefetch_evict_count, sensitivity_mismatch_alerts (when high-sensitivity requests experienced host hits).
